name: Hook 1.mp4
speech: Itchy skin at night can be a sign of something worse.
Watch this before you buy another tube of cream.
So I'm 58. I didn't think I had allergies, but my skin had been giving me a lot of trouble.
Every night when I got into bed it started. My arms, my neck, the backs of my legs.
I'd often wake up scratching and by morning my nose was blocked and my eyes were puffy.
This had been going on for quite a long time and I'd had enough. I was ready to find out what was
going on. My doctor had already checked my skin. Overall nothing too impressive. A little dryness,
a little irritation, nothing unusual for my age. But with my symptoms I had a sneaky suspicion I
knew what was going on. So I looked at what lives inside a mattress and it looked a little something
like this. A mattress like mine can hold anywhere from 100,000 to 10 million dust mites. What does
this mean? Basically dust mites live in the fabric of your mattress where they feed on the skin you
shed every night. Every mite leaves about 20 droppings a day, loaded with an allergen called
Derpy One. And you lie in it for eight hours a night. This can build up for a few reasons. An older
mattress, a warm humid bedroom, years of shed skin packed into the fabric. Some homes are just
more humid than others. Either way it explained why everything was worst in bed. I looked at my
options. There are antihistamines and creams for relief. There's replacing the mattress,
but a new one starts filling right back up from your pillows and your own skin within a few months.
But ultimately the best thing I found was to get them out of the mattress with capture cards.
Dust mites have no eyes. They follow scent. Capture cards give off a plant-derived pheromone
lure that reaches into the fabric they hide in and pulls them onto the card where the adhesive
holds them. It doesn't kill them where they are because a dead mite carries the same allergen as a
live one. It brings them out. For comparison, sprays and vacuums only reach the top layer.
I was skeptical, understandably, after dealing with this for so long. But I gave it a real shot
before buying a new mattress. One card under the mattress, one near my pillow. Six weeks later,
for me, the itching at night had noticeably eased. My mornings were clearer. My sleep was better too.
I'm so happy with my results and I wish I'd found it sooner.
